results.gene_summary: glnA :: glutamine synthetase, type I :: Involved in nitrogen metabolism via ammonium assimilation. Catalyzes the ATP-dependent biosynthesis of glutamine from glutamate and ammonia
results.function_description: Involved in nitrogen metabolism via ammonium assimilation. Catalyzes the ATP-dependent biosynthesis of glutamine from glutamate and ammonia

discussed_in_publications.evidence: The larger NtcA iModulon includes ntcA, glutamate synthase (glnA), glnB (Results 2.4, lines 193-195)

Members of the NtcA regulon that exhibited increased transcript abundance during N-deprivation included genes encoding the assimilation pathways for urea and cyanate, as well as the glutamine synthase gene glnA (Supplementary Tables S3–S6). (p5, Results)
The glnA gene, encoding GS, was upregulated in both strains (Figure 4D), similar to other cyanobacteria (Results, p7)

experiments.design_notes: Each timepoint (day 18, day 31, day 60, day 89, days 60+89) is coculture MED4 vs the same coculture series sampled on day 11 (exponential). days 60+89 pools the day 60 and day 89 samples.

day 14, day 31 and day 89: axenic MED4 vs axenic MED4 sampled on day 7 (exponential). Day 7 and day 14 come from the axenic repeat experiment; the methods do not say which run day 31 and day 89 came from.
Each timepoint (day 18, day 31, day 60, day 89) is coculture MED4 vs the same coculture series sampled on day 11 (exponential). days 60+89 pools the day 60 and day 89 samples.

Control for 2h and 4h is the normal-diel circadian time-course sample at the same ZT (ZT 2 and ZT 4, lights on, diel), not ZT 0 as one Methods sentence suggests; the reported log2FC reproduce the same-ZT contrast from the GEO GSE314951 counts (r = 1.00) and not the ZT 0 contrast (r below 0.6).
Dark and light arms come from two experiments run on separate days, each split from its own mid-log (exponential) mother culture; arms are compared at the same hours post-inoculation.

Matched by growth state, not by sampling day: the axenic MED4 control came from a separate repeat experiment sampled on days 7 and 14 to match axenic MED4 growth dynamics (Methods p. 14). day 11: coculture day 11 vs axenic day 7 (both exponential). day 18: coculture day 18 vs axenic day 14 (death, axenic MED4 lost viability around day 11).
day 14: axenic MED4 vs the same axenic series sampled on day 7 (exponential); axenic MED4 was a separate repeat experiment sampled on days 7 and 14. No axenic MED4 RNA exists after day 14.

steady state: log-phase cultures acclimated to the alternative N source vs log-phase cultures on ammonium (exponential). Methods do not state that both arms were harvested on the same day; matched by growth state, assumed from the acclimated parallel-culture design.

max across 70min-24h: gas-shocked and air-sparged control bottles were split from one pooled culture at t = 0 and sampled in parallel at the same times (exponential). The value is the extremum over time of the log2 change versus t = 0 under the gas minus the same change in air; significance by betr against the parallel air time course.

max across 70min-24h: gas-shocked and air-sparged control bottles were split from one pooled culture at t = 0 and sampled in parallel at the same times (exponential). The value is the extremum over time of the log2 change versus t = 0 under the gas minus the same change in air; significance by betr against the parallel air time course.

max across 70min-24h: the air-sparged culture at each time is compared with its own t = 0 sample (taken immediately after centrifugation and resuspension, before sparging; exponential). Table S1 reports the maximal log2 fold change versus t = 0 over the time course; significance by betr time-series test against t = 0.

Control for 14h and 16h is the normal-diel circadian time-course sample at the same ZT (ZT 14 and ZT 16, lights off, diel), not ZT 0 or ZT 12; the reported log2FC reproduce the same-ZT contrast from the GEO GSE314951 counts (r = 1.00) and not the ZT 12 contrast (r below 0.82).
